newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sappi shares slide on poor year results.
newsitem.headline: Sappi shares slide on poor year results.

text.p: Shares in South African paper and pulp producer Sappi lost over two percent on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Tuesday shortly after the release of worse-than-expected year results, dealers said.
They said there was, however, some support for the stock which had helped it off its lowest levels of the morning.
"The losses are purely on the results," said a trader at a large brokerage firm.
"But there is two-way thought on the share with some people saying the losses are already in the price and that the paper market on the commodity side is bottoming out."
The other view was that the results were worse-than-expected and that Sappi still had many problems with production efficiency and management to sort out, he said.
Sappi on Tuesday reported earnings for the year to end-September falling 73 percent to 230 cents a share from 846 cents a year ago mainly due to weak pulp and paper demand and prices.
Shares lost 2.4 percent or 100 cents to 41 rand shortly after the start of trading, but by 0800 GMT had recovered to 41.25 rand -- a 75 cents drop.
Dealers said the share's fall was expected to be capped at the 40 rand level.
"We are saying sell at current levels, but we see people becoming cautious buyers below 40 rand," another trader said.
